data.title: UniFirst finishes FTC information request, parties evaluate remedies - CTFN
data.description:
UniFirst  (UNF) has finished the data compilation needed by the Federal Trade Commission as the regulator evaluates its sale to Cintas (CTAS).

Cintas (CTSA) is still working to complete its part and expects a full submission by no later than the end of November for an end-of-year deal close, according to a CTFN report that was circulating on Friday, which cited an unidentified source. The parties want to complete their submission soon, as they expect remedy talks with the FTC.

Both companies expect the regulator will ask for a remedy, with the parties possibly giving an upfront proposal to try to stay on the timeline, according to the report. It wasn't known what the possible concessions or remedies might be.

Uniform retail firm Cintas (CTAS)  agreed to acquire smaller rival UniFirst (UNF) for $310 per share in cash and stock in March, representing an enterprise value of about $5.5B.

The UniFirst (UNF) deal spread has widened to $52 on Friday from around $20 in early August as investors appear to be concerned that the FTC could sue to block the transaction.

data.title: Integra LifeSciences plunges 21% on preliminary Q3 results
data.description:
Shares of Integra LifeSciences (IART), a global medical technology company focused on neurosurgery, surgical instrumentation, and regenerative technologies, retreated almost 21% on Friday. This came after the company released preliminary third-quarter results alongside a proposed $600 million debt refinancing.

IART ended at $12.68, down $3.41 from its previous close, with trading volume running at roughly 2.6 times the one-month average.

data.title: SA Asks: Does AMD still have upside after its latest rally? (Update)
data.description:
(Article updated to add commentary from Jack Bowman.)

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) have rallied 40% over the last 30 days, hitting a new 52-week high this week. 

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Jack Bowman, Danil Sereda, The Value Portfolio, and Fundamental Options if they thought the stock still had significant upside following its most recent rally.

Jack Bowman: I'm still a semiconductor bull at this point, so generally speaking, yes. More specifically, AMD's (AMD) earnings are real and growing quickly; it justifies the high PE ratio. All the money in AI is currently flowing to chipmakers, and that doesn't look like it's changing anytime soon. AMD has run up significantly, and it's got a nearly 40x FWD PE ratio, but I think it's justified. 

It's difficult to compete with AMD, and the only other chipmaker that can is 5x the market cap. Nvidia (NVDA) also makes significantly more revenue, to be fair, but AMD is growing fast and has always benefited from its position as a plucky underdog. The market loves its narrative. 

More succinctly, AMD (AMD) looks more likely to continue higher than go lower, at least in the medium term.

Danil Sereda: I wrote an update on AMD a few days ago, downgrading the stock back to Hold from my previous Buy rating. My reasoning is simple: I don't see any sufficient margin of safety anymore after the massive run-up in price. 

I agree with the bulls that AMD's (AMD) operational execution and data center momentum remain strong, with FY2027 server CPU growth projected at over 70% year-over-year and TAM estimates rising sharply. Plus, the agentic AI opportunity is still very early, and it's hard to quantify it just yet. 

AMD's growth might happen to be above today's consensus growth rates in two to three years. But at current high-end consensus estimates for FY2028, AMD trades at 6–8x sales. I don't think it's reasonably cheap for the sector, considering my bullishness in the core assumptions regarding the consensus figures taken. 

The most reasonable rating is a Hold now, in my opinion.

(Danil Sereda leads the SA investing group Beyond the Wall Investing.)

The Value Portfolio: I don't think AMD (AMD) still has upside after its latest rally. The firm has an incredibly lofty valuation to grow into, well above peers like Nvidia (NVDA). 

Furthermore, its largest customer, Meta (META), whose deal involved substantial equity, is now working with Broadcom (AVGO) to build custom silicon, the same custom silicon peers like Google (GOOG) (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN) have scaled into the gigawatts. 

We think it's a matter of time before Meta (META) does the same, which will compress AMD's margins and stop its ability to grow into its valuation.

(The Value Portfolio leads SA investing group The Retirement Forum.)

Fundamental Options: In a base-case scenario, where I tried to be a bit on the conservative side, the DCF fair value that I estimated for AMD (AMD) a few days ago was $553. In a pessimistic scenario, with reduced TAM for GPUs and server CPUs and lower perpetual growth, the fair value would be around $395. In an optimistic scenario, with a higher perpetual growth rate and a lower discount rate, the fair value would be $733; if we add higher TAM and market share, then $800+.

While I can't assign exact probabilities to the three scenarios, the chances are more or less evenly distributed, but likely with a slight edge for the optimistic scenario, as I tried to be a bit conservative in my base case. Significant upside potential exists only in the optimistic scenario. In the base case scenario, once the fair value reaches the current price in approximately one year, an annual growth of ~10.5% (the discount rate) would follow.

I gradually trimmed part of my position following sharp gains to protect myself against the pessimistic scenario. I’m holding a portion to benefit from the optimistic scenario. I hedged the remaining portion for the base-case scenario.

data.title: MaxLinear climbs 15% amid infrastructure and data-center focus
data.description:
MaxLinear (MXL), a fabless semiconductor designer, rallied just over 15% on Friday, closing at $105.93 after gaining $13.81 on the day.

The gain extended a recovery that has built over the past several weeks, as the company's infrastructure and data-center product lines drew renewed investor attention. Volume reached approximately 4.28 million shares, nearly one and a half times the one-month average.

MXL has advanced about 87% over the past month. This included periodic strong one-session gains, including a 10% rise on September 25 and advances of about 8% on both September 17 and 18.

data.title: Nike seeks supply chain overhaul to improve profitability -- report
data.description:
Still reeling from the fallout from disappointing fiscal first-quarter results and another turn lower in the company’s share price, Nike (NKE) is now exploring ways to improve profitability by streamlining its supply chain and breaking with a 50-year trend of owning its own distribution network.

During a meeting with employees on Friday cited by Bloomberg, Nike (NKE) COO Venky Alagirisamy said the company aims to make a “more flexible, more responsive, and more efficient supply chain” and move towards a model to “leverage partnerships.”

Alagirisamy added that while manufacturing in Vietnam and China will remain "significant," Nike (NKE) is looking to "nearshore" sourcing for its North America and EMEA markets, a strategy the company had previously discussed prior to Thursday’s results.

While profits improved during the fiscal first quarter, the gains came from cost efficiencies rather than higher sales, momentum that could be interrupted by the recent spike in oil futures and its likely impact on transportation costs. By moving manufacturing closer to end markets, Nike (NKE) can mitigate the volatility in transportation costs. 

During the company’s earnings call with analysts, chief financial officer David Denton noted efforts to improve efficiencies, simplify operations, and increase productivity by “directing more resources towards the consumer, sport, product innovation, and growth opportunities with the greatest long-term potential.”

Nike (NKE) shares ended lower for a fourth consecutive day.
